title: YOLO-MS: Rethinking Multi-Scale Representation Learning for Real-time Object Detection

problem.summary: The paper argues that real-time detectors still handle scale poorly: multi-branch CSP/ELAN blocks produce homogenized inter-branch features, Res2Net-style hierarchy leaks contaminative spatial information, and homogeneous per-stage kernel sizes prevent cheap use of large receptive fields.
statements: Inter-branch features in popular CSP and ELAN blocks are homogenized, so multi-scale information is not truly diverse.
Hierarchical multi-branch blocks (Res2Net) enrich diversity but inject spatial information unrelated to the target object.
Prior real-time detectors use the same kernel size in every stage, limiting large-kernel convolutions and effective receptive fields.

evidence.quote: recognizing objects at different scales remains a fundamental challenge for real-time object detectors.
their inter-branch features are homogenized, reflecting a potential absence of diverse multi-scale information.
it introduces contaminative spatial information as shown in Fig. 1, not related to the target object, potentially harming detection performance.
However, the kernel size only reaches 5 × 5 due to speed limitation. Homogeneous block design in different stages limits the application of largekernel convolutions.

background.summary: The work builds on FPN/PAFPN necks, the CSP/ELAN real-time line (YOLOv4-v7, RTMDet), the Res2Net hierarchical block, and large-kernel CNN studies, claiming prior work improved neck macro-structures while neglecting multi-scale learning inside the basic building blocks.

relatedWork.name: FPN / PAFPN
relatedWork.relation: prior multi-scale fusion necks the paper builds its pyramid on
relatedWork.quote: Typically, FPN [41], PAFPN [45], and GatherDistribute mechanism [64] modify the model neck to improve the aggregation of different scale features.

relatedWork.name: RTMDet
relatedWork.relation: baseline detector and prior large-kernel adopter
relatedWork.quote: RTMDet [48] first introduces large-kernel convolutions (5×5) into networks to boost the feature extraction capability of the CSP block.

relatedWork.name: Res2Net
relatedWork.relation: source of the hierarchical multi-branch structure used in MS-Block
relatedWork.quote: This hierarchical multi-branch structure is the key of Res2Net [14] to augment the richness of information at different scales in building blocks.

relatedWork.name: RT-DETR
relatedWork.relation: transformer-based real-time alternative that removes NMS
relatedWork.quote: RT-DETR [80] constructs the first transformer-based model to avoid the negative impact of NMS at inference time.

evidence.quote: The wider receptive field provided by large-kernel convolutions can be a potent technique for building strong multi-scale feature representations

However, the mainstream of the basic building block overlooks the importance of multi-scale feature representation learning while focusing on how to facilitate detection efficiency or how to introduce new training techniques

solution.summary: The paper replaces CSP/ELAN blocks with an MS-Block that hierarchically splits features across branches re-weighted by a lightweight Global Query Learning module, and applies a Heterogeneous Kernel Size Selection protocol that grows kernel sizes 3, 5, 7, 9 from shallow to deep stages.
solution.approach: Hierarchical multi-branch MS-Blocks with a shared global query (GQL) plus a stage-wise increasing kernel-size schedule (HKS) to enrich multi-scale feature representation at real-time cost.
components: Global Query Learning (GQL) with a shared lightweight query
PAFPN neck and head built from MS-Blocks

evidence.quote: we propose an efficient strategy named Global Query Learning (GQL), aiming at offering cross-stage guidance for basic blocks.
we maintain a global query that stores the cross-stage spatial representations of each branch.
the kernel sizes of convolutions are 3, 5, 7, and 9 from the shallowest to the deepest stage.
we gradually increase the kernel size from lower stages to higher ones.

experiments.summary: The authors train three YOLO-MS scales from scratch on COCO for 300 epochs in MMDetection, ablate GQL, HKS, branch number and query dimension against RTMDet, compare with SOTA real-time detectors, and extend to instance segmentation, DOTA oriented detection, CrowdHuman, underwater, foggy and RAW-image detection.

evidence.quote: YOLO-MS-XS reaches 42.8% AP, which is 1.8% AP higher than it with the ImageNet [8] pre-trained model.
our proposed methods bring a significant improvement of +1.8% AP compared to RTMDet.
our method advances the AP of YOLOv8-N, YOLOv8-S, and YOLOv8-M from 37.2%, 43.9%, and 49.8% to 40.2%, 46.2%, and 50.6%, respectively.
the segmentation AP of our YOLOMS increases from 40.5% to 42.8% with an improvement of +2.3%.

limitations.summary: Branch richness is throttled by speed (the better-scoring 4-branch variant is slower), adding branches does not help monotonically, and the largest model had to be trained with a reduced batch size for hardware reasons.
items: Default Nb = 3 sacrifices accuracy of the Nb = 4 variant for higher FPS (150 vs 137).
Increasing branch count or query size does not monotonically improve AP.
Large version trained with batch size 16 per GPU due to hardware limits.
All results rely on a single from-scratch recipe (300 epochs, MMDetection, 640x640 input).

evidence.quote: If the speed is not an obstacle, Nb = 4 is also recommended.
directly increasing the size of branches does not always lead to performance improvement.
due to the hardware limitation, the batch size for the large version model is 16 per GPU

applications.detail: Real-time detectors are stated to be deployed in industry on edge devices such as drones and robotics.
applications.quote: have found significant applications in industries, particularly for edge devices, such as drones and robotics.

applications.detail: YOLO-MS-R variants are evaluated on DOTA-v1.0 aerial oriented detection, where objects are typically small.
applications.quote: objects in remote sensing scenarios are typically small

applications.detail: YOLO-MS is evaluated on CrowdHuman for detecting people in crowded scenes.
applications.quote: Detecting objects in crowded scenarios is also a crucial topic in computer vision.

deploymentClaims: YOLO-MS-XS measured at 7.1 ms latency, 5.1M params and 8.7G MACs at 640x640 in the common benchmark environment (Table 8).
FPS benchmarked on an NVIDIA 3090 GPU in FP32; the ablation tiny model runs at 150 FPS (Table 3).
FPS evaluation performed without NMS post-processing, batch size 1.

During testing, we perform inference without the NMS postprocessing step
